This radical is the same as the kanji. It means right .

If you loiter around the sun temple , it's likely you'll acquire something. When you loiter around like that it looks like you're waiting for something, so if someone puts something in your hands and you just happen to acquire it, well, no one can fault you for that. Hints Imagine loitering around near the sun temple. Maybe you acquire some illegal goods, maybe you just acquire a tan (it is a SUN temple, after all).
readingMnemonic: You managed to acquire some tobacco, but just as you're about to leave Toku gawa ( とく ) Ieyasu comes marching up to you!! Or at least, his ghost does. He stares you dead in the eyes and says, "I didn't found the shogunate for you to acquire illegal goods and kill your body toking on my soil." Hints Your eyes fill with tears under Tokugawa's gaze and you drop everything you acquired to the ground. You bow before him apologizing. You'll never do this again!

meaningMnemonic: The power of your mouth lets you add words together to form a sentence. Marvel at the mighty additive power your mouth holds! You add words together in an amazing fashion! Hints Say this sentence out loud. Incredible! You've used the power of your mouth to add words together in a sentence. Your parents must be very proud of you.
readingMnemonic: Your parents are so proud of you being able to add words together that they surprise you with a new ca r ( か ). Wow! You add some stickers to your bumper and add your favorite playlist to the car radio. Let's drive. Hints Imagine riding around in your new car, singing songs with your powerful mouth to the playlists you added to the fancy new radio.

meaningMnemonic: You use a bookshelf as a book counter . Duh. What, are you gonna count them one by one? Okay, well maybe, but you should count them while they're nice and organized on the shelves. Otherwise counting is going to be a huge pain. Hints Imagine counting books on a bunch of bookshelves. One book, two book, red book, blue book!
readingMnemonic: You use this book counter method to count all the books Satsu ki ( さつ ) has in her house. Remember her? She's got, like, a ton of books, but she's just a little girl so she needs some help. That's where your book counter know-how comes in handy. Hints Imagine how tedious it'd be to watch her counting one by one. Teach her your book counter ways!

meaningMnemonic: The dirt next to your village is where you bury the dead. People don't live forever, so every village has a patch of dirt specifically used for burying dead things. Hints Imagine the village where you grew up. Can you see the dirt area where all your ancestors were buried?
readingMnemonic: You don't just bury dead relatives here. You also buried your dead pet u ni ( う ) in that dirt. You thought having an uni as a pet would be a good idea. Too bad uni need water to survive. Hints Imagine crying as you bury your pet uni. Your tears can't save it now. (Though it is a bit ironic, since it needed salt water.)

meaningMnemonic: You'll work your soul to death if you're too busy . Being busy just isn't good for your soul. Take breaks. Go on vacation. Don't be so busy that you destroy yourself. Hints Look around you. See all those busy people? Their souls are dying. Don't end up like them.
readingMnemonic: Take time out of your busy life and go bow ling ( ぼう ) once in a while. In fact, you should probably go bowling once a week at least. Nothing brings energy back to your life like some relaxing bowling. Hints Think about your busy schedule this week. Now cancel everything and just go bowling instead.

meaningMnemonic: Passed out in front of your gate lies a former leader . He's now a drunkard , but once ran a popular clique called the Cool Kids Clan . The clan has fallen apart, and he no longer has a clique to call his own. Hints Imagine this washed up drunkard leader passed out in front of the gate to your house. You have to pass him whenever you enter or exit your house. He's gross and he smells. Experience the stench in your nostrils. How he was ever the leader of a clan you have no idea.
readingMnemonic: Eventually you get sick and tired of this washed up clan leader and you gather your own clique to chase this guy away from your gate and your property. You and your friends grab some bats ( ばつ ) and use these bats to beat the drunkard leader. Being beaten with bats frightens him, and he scurries away. Hints Hear the crushing blows of bats against flesh as you imagine this scene in your mind. You're beating the crap out of this guy with a bunch of bats, but hey — he had it coming.

meaningMnemonic: To a narwhal , a towel is just normal cloth . They're always wet so towel cloth is all they know. Hints Picture a narwhal wrapped in a fuzzy towel blanket, with a towel tail cover, and some towel underpants. Everything is made of this type of cloth.
readingMnemonic: If you use this type of cloth for your clothes and blankets people will call you a foo l ( ふ ). They think you're a fool who can't tell the difference between human cloth and towel cloth. Hints "You fool, you aren't a narwhal, that cloth isn't for you!" they say. They're so mean.

meaningMnemonic: You have to gather thread to sell if you want to continue living. You want to make a living, don't you? Make sure you continue to sell that thread every single day! Hints Imagine selling thread so you can continue living. You search for thread continually now. But are you gathering thread to continue to live, or living to continue gathering thread?
readingMnemonic: You have to continue to sell that thread because a Boso zoku ( ぞく ) bike gang is forcing you to do it. You see? If you want to continue to live, you have to appease this Bosozoku gang. You better keep selling! Hints Continue selling thread and paying off the Bosozoku. It's the only way you can continue to survive!

meaningMnemonic: Direct a tsunami into a canine 's mouth to decrease the amount of water that strikes the surrounding area. Hints Just make sure you get a really thirsty canine, because they're going to need to drink a LOT of water to decrease the tsunami's power.
readingMnemonic: After you and your canine decrease the tsunami's power, Gen ji ( げん ) comes out to thank you. That tsunami was on track to wash away Genji's house, which would have forced him to majorly decrease his frivolous playboy activities. Hints Now you're wondering if you made the right choice. The world might actually be a better place if Genji decreased his silly lover-boy antics a bit.

meaningMnemonic: The easy radical and the easy kanji are the same! Hints Easy is easy!
readingMnemonic: What would be an easy reading for this kanji? い ! The sound easy starts with! Hints I told you easy was easy.

meaningMnemonic: If you put a thread in the middle of a kiss , you’re going to entangle it. Things can get pretty messy in a kiss, so adding a thread to the mix will definitely entangle it. Hints Imagine trying to kiss someone with a piece of thread between your lips. Feel the thread getting all entangled between the two of you. Thread entangled, tongues entangled, lips entangled — just a thready kiss of entanglement.
readingMnemonic: This isn't going well, so you pull out the weird kiss thread and entangle it around a rack ( らく ). Good thing that rack was there! Much better to have it entangled around a rack when you're trying to kiss someone. Hints Imagine pausing this kiss to pull a thread out of your mouth and entangle it around a random rack in your room. Smooth move, Casanova! Your partner will totally love that.

meaningMnemonic: Within the bamboo grove, someone asks your reason for being there, and you explain it's to harvest bamboo to craft a flute . Hints Imagine yourself cutting down some bamboo, thinking, "This is the reason I'm here, I need a flute, ASAP!" There is no other reason to be here besides this.
readingMnemonic: You cut down the bamboo and whittle a flute . You start playing a song. You know the reason why. An alien spacecraft comes flying down and drops a box full of alien tech ( てき ) in front of you. Hints You've done what you came to do. You summoned an alien craft with your bamboo flute, gaining some alien tech in the process. Open up the box to see what tech awaits you.

meaningMnemonic: If you put a roof over a valley it will change its form . Its appearance will alter completely! Hints Picture a valley in your mind. Now put a roof on it. Hmm. It isn't shape d like a valley anymore.
readingMnemonic: Its new appearance looks familiar to you, like it's a big yo gurt ( よう ) cup! A valley with a roof on it looks exactly like a yogurt cup. Huh! Hints Now imagine this taking shape before your eyes and becoming actual yogurt! You grab a giant spoon and take a bite.

meaningMnemonic: Use your mouth to take a measurement of this group . Just stretch your mouth out and around every single person. Get 'em all in there. Hints I hope this group is full of people who enjoy being inside someone else's mouth, because they're gonna be pretty mad when you let them out if they aren't.
readingMnemonic: This group is so big it takes you till dawn ( だん ) to get your measurement: they weigh a ton ( とん ) too! Hints Imagine letting this group of, now very wet, people out of your mouth one by one. They don't seem to care that they weigh a ton! That's a large measurement, they should be proud.

meaningMnemonic: If the sun is compare d to an insect , you’ll see that they're both shiny, but that the sun is much shinier than the insect. Hints Imagine holding up an insect to the sun to compare the two. See how they both shine, but the sun shines more brightly than the insect.
readingMnemonic: While you’re holding up an insect to the sun for comparison, a flock of con dors ( こん ) flies by, blocking out the sun. There are so many condors that they manage to totally block out the sun. Hints Feel how dark and cold it is suddenly with all those condors blocking out the sun.

meaningMnemonic: “Don’t loiter – run , Junior !” said Indiana Jones Senior to Indiana Jones Junior. They’re escaping from a sticky situation and Junior was just loitering around like a fool. It’s no time to loiter, it’s time to run! Hints Imagine Sean Connery saying “Don’t loiter – run, Junior!” and you should have a much easier time remembering this phrase if you remember it in his voice.
readingMnemonic: Deciding not to loiter any longer, Indiana Jones Junior takes his dad’s advice and starts to run. Unfortunately he wasn’t paying attention to where his feet were and he stubbed his to e ( と ) on a jagged rock. His toe is in so much pain that he can’t bear to run any longer. Hints Imagine that you are Indiana Jones Junior and this is happening to you. Feel the terrible pain of your throbbing toe as you clutch it, with the bad guys catching up with you.

meaningMnemonic: You jumped off your roof for some reason and now you're floating in midair ! You kick your legs a bit and move your arms like you're in water, but you're still just stuck there in midair. Hints At the moment you can't remember the reason you did it, but when you jumped off your roof you just floated in midair.
readingMnemonic: As you spin a bit in midair you look up and see Chew bacca ( ちゅう ) looking down at you from a spaceship. He's laughing his Chewbacca laugh and you realize he has you trapped in his tractor beam. Hints Oh Chewbacca, you lovable fuzzball. You better not drop me in midair, or I'll die. I hope you bring me up there!

meaningMnemonic: A raging tsunami rises next to the calm sun . When you try to compare these two things, it's clear that they cannot mix . If a tsunami is coming, it will likely get in the way of the sun. Hints Imagine the sun getting blocked out as a tsunami rises up from the ocean. Feel the cold fear of death on you as the tsunami approaches. That tsunami is gonna mix you up.
readingMnemonic: Just before the tsunami crashes over you, a con dor ( こん ) swoops out of the sky and grabs you up. This condor must be a mix — a normal condor is not strong enough to pick up a human. The condor must be mixed with something else. Like a pterodactyl. Hints Imagine yourself getting mixed up in this situation and the pterodactyl-sized condor picking you up. Feel the condor's talons digging into your shoulders as it grabs you up and flies you towards the sun.

meaningMnemonic: A sheep loses its horns on the ground so it picks them up in its mouth to take them to someone who's morally good enough to attach them back onto its head. Sheep don’t have hands, so the sheep had to pick the horns up off the ground with his mouth. Someone evil would just murder the sheep and steal his horns, so the sheep must find someone good to reaffix them. Hints Imagine yourself as the good person being approached by this forlorn sheep without horns. Hear the clack of the horns together as the sheep drops them out of his mouth onto the ground and lets out a pathetic bleat. “Baa~aa~ah~”
readingMnemonic: Since you are morally good , you decide not to murder the sheep and harvest its organs. Instead, as a practitioner of the good teachings of Zen ( ぜん ) Buddhism, you decided to help the sheep out. Your Zen teachings have increased the power of your healing abilities, so you fix the sheep up in no time. Hints Imagine yourself using your Zen magic to heal this sheep. Place your hands on the sheep’s horns and imagine returning them to their rightful location on the sheep’s head. Feel the soft wool of the sheep as he bleats in happiness.

meaningMnemonic: When they migrate to a river , a group of geoducks must do so in a certain order and sequence . Hints Geoducks usually live in the ocean, but when they migrate to a river, they do so in a specific, predetermined order. Imagine what that sequence might be. Maybe in order of neck length, with the longest-necked geoducks going first? Or maybe in alphabetical order?
readingMnemonic: Actually, they go in birth-month order , starting from June ( じゅん ). No one knows why they follow this June-based sequence . But the geoducks born in June always go first in the migration order. Hints Imagine it's June, and you're on a beach somewhere watching a bunch of geoducks make their way to a river. Marvel at the biological clock that determines the June-based migration sequence for these fascinating creatures.

meaningMnemonic: You use a roof to keep yourself dry and safe from outer space . Look outside, above your roof, and you'll see outer space stretching above you. Hints You don't want to float up into outer space and get all wet, do you? No? Then you better make sure you have a roof above your head.
readingMnemonic: Why isn't it dry in outer space , you ask? Because of all the u ni ( う ) swimming around up there. They have nasty, wet, pointy spikes and they're all over the place. Hints Look closely up at outer space and you'll see all of the uni floating around up there. They're really dark, so it can be hard to notice them, but I promise you, they're there.

meaningMnemonic: What you say to the director is judged immediately. You're having trouble understanding this part of speech , so he's trying to help you. But you say it over and over and he keeps saying you're wrong. Hints "Is it an adjective?" "No, that's the wrong part of speech." "Is it a verb?" "N-no! Of course not!"
readingMnemonic: The director asks you again, "What is the part of speech for the word shee p ( し )?" Hints You stare blankly at him. What part of speech is that?! It's an animal, you know that. Oh! A noun. Duh.

meaningMnemonic: If you see some flowers that are dry , pull them up and you'll find a potato . Hints Potatoes grow when flowers dry out. All the nutrients are going to the potato under the ground, so the flowers up top get sucked dry.
readingMnemonic: Potato es are totally emo ( いも ) because of the way they dry out flowers. Emo people and potatoes both like to dry out flowers. Hints Picture an emo person sitting alone in a dark room, staring at a potato. "You and I are the same."

meaningMnemonic: It's important to focus oneself in winter so that one can emerge renew ed! You can't really go outside in winter without getting cold or sick, so spend winter focusing on YOU. Hints Imagine sitting in your house all winter, meditating and thinking about how you can renew yourself.
readingMnemonic: Winter ends and, renew ed, you come out ready to start a new hobby: kay aking ( かい )! Nothing says renewal like a brand new kayak and sense of purpose in life. Hints Imagine being back in your house in winter. You're thinking about all the kayaking you're gonna do when winter ends. You're even making the movements with your arms, so you'll be a really renewed you.

meaningMnemonic: You loiter around a black hole , waiting for it to finish destroying stuff so you can switch it to restore mode. You were told all black holes finish eventually, and when they do you can press a button to restore everything back to the way it was. Hints Imagine loitering around near (but not too near!) the black hole, waiting for it to finish so you can restore the galaxy.
readingMnemonic: When there's nothing else for the black hole to eat, you hit the restore button.... but nothing happens. "Oh, f**k ( ふく ) you!" you scream, as you realize you were lied to. Hints Maybe if you yell f**k you enough things will be restored. Ha. No. Everything's gone and it's your fault for being gullible.

meaningMnemonic: If you stab somebody in the tongue with an umbrella , it’s sure to start a riot and cause disorder . Nobody likes to get stabbed in the tongue with an umbrella, so they’re probably going to retaliate, and before you know it, you’ve a full scale riot on your hands. Look what you’ve done. Hints Imagine yourself getting stabbed in the tongue with an umbrella. It’s very painful. Taste the blood and metal in your mouth as this happens to you.
readingMnemonic: Just now you realize that the man you stabbed in the tongue with your umbrella was none other than Macho Man Ran dy Savage ( らん ). Being a professional wrestler, Macho Man Randy Savage is ready to throw down at a moment’s notice. A riot immediately erupts. It’s a battle royal with you and Randy at the epicenter. Hints Picture yourself squaring off with Macho Man Randy Savage in the middle of this riot. You have the advantage of having an umbrella, but Randy has the advantage of being himself. Picture yourself getting into a fight with him.

meaningMnemonic: On the bottom of bamboo root s, there’s a stamp that tells you the season in which it was cut. Additionally, the stamp also has information on the condition of the bamboo’s joint s, because no one wants to buy bamboo with damaged joints! Hints Picture yourself in a store, looking at a bunch of different bamboo stamps to make sure you don’t buy one that’s out of season, or one that has damaged joints. The season and the joints, that’s what quality bamboo is all about, and it’s why we have these stamps!
readingMnemonic: These season stamps are marked on bamboo sets ( せつ ). You can't buy a single banana or a single grape, and just like that, if you want some nice seasonal bamboo, you have to buy them in sets. Hints How many bamboo sets will you be buying this season? I'm getting 42 sets.

meaningMnemonic: Your scooter and your car is what you always take along with you. Make sure they're connect ed well so you don't lose them! Hints Your scooter and your car, connected by a tiny little string, are the two things you take along with you wherever you go.
readingMnemonic: You take along your scooter and your car. Anything else, you can do a ren tal ( れん ) for! Hints The roof over your head? Rental. The clothes on your body? Rental. All of your friends? Rental. The only thing you permanently take along with you are your scooter and your car.

meaningMnemonic: The tongue radical and the tongue kanji are exactly the same! Yee-haw!
readingMnemonic: You’re sound asleep in bed when your tongue drops out of your mouth and you start to drool, getting saliva all over the bed sheet ( した ). You wake up with a soggy patch of sheet near your mouth and wipe the drool off your face. Your significant other sees the whole thing. Hints Your significant other had been watching you sleep with your tongue out for a while now, so you're super embarrassed you wet the sheets with your nasty tongue drool. You feel very judged and embarrassed.

meaningMnemonic: When the sun gets together with water , only violence can ensue. They don’t mix well together. The sun loves to fight water and water loves to fight the sun. Lots and lots of violence. Hints Picture this violent fight scene in your brain. Imagine water locked in battle with the sun as the sun’s fire flares up and the water starts to sizzle.
readingMnemonic: But after a while, the sun and the water have had enough of violence . They decide to settle their differences with a friendly game of bow ling ( ぼう ). Bowling is a great way to relieve stress and in the end, they bond over it. Hints Imagine the sun and the water trying to bowl. Hear the sound of bowling balls rolling down the lane and pins rattling around and crashing together.

meaningMnemonic: Give some shellfish to a talent ed person and they'll have no problem accumulating wealth . People with talent can make money out of pretty much anything, so shellfish are like easy-mode. Hints Picture the talented person huddled over a pile of shellfish, whispering to them about the wealth they'll soon be turned into.
readingMnemonic: This talented person really starts accumulating wealth when their cy borg ( さい ) is unveiled. It's a half-man, half-shellfish cyborg that plays the xy lophone  ( ざい ), and everyone wants to buy it. Hints You'd be wealthy too if you sold that cyborg you made. It may not have any shellfish in it and it can't play the xylophone, but you could change that…

meaningMnemonic: There are flowers on your right to show that you're still young . Your body still works, you're happy, you have your entire life ahead of you! And everything smells like flowers. Hints Look to your right, if you see flowers (metaphorically, maybe) then you're still young. Congratulations!
readingMnemonic: When young people look to the right, they'll see their future: a walke r ( わか ). You know, those metal contraptions with tennis balls on the bottoms to make sure they don't scrape the floor. Everything may be flowers and happiness now, but your future is in a walker. Hints All young people have a walker looming just off to the side. A sign that your youth won't last forever, dear summer child.

meaningMnemonic: A part of speech that creates the shape and form of a word is something that is descriptive (its shape and form are in there, after all!). This shape and form part of speech is an adjective . You are so beautiful!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

meaningMnemonic: This is a little confusing for someone who didn't grow up with the Japanese language. You have fifty sound s. Then, they're in a certain order . So, these fifty sounds are the Japanese syllabary. That's hiragana / katakana, probably from back in the day when there were more sounds than there are now. So, the "fifty sounds in order" makes up aiueo order , where the "aiueo" is あいうえお representing the five columns.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

meaningMnemonic: If something happens in the east , west , south , and north , then it's happening in all directions . What other directions are there? That's literally all of them. meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. meaningMnemonic: Well, well, look at this — another verb for the pass through kanji! You've already learned 通る (to pass through) and 通う (to visit regularly), but this one adds another nuance. It means to get through to , with an emphasis on going from point A to point B via a particular route. 通じる is used for lots of different things involving people and places being linked, or things being conveyed from one point to another. Whether it's a road leading to a certain city, a phone call reaching its recipient, or words or feelings getting across to someone, the emphasis is all on connection and transmission.
readingMnemonic: Like other verbs that end in じる , this actually uses the on'yomi of the kanji, not kun'yomi! You learned that reading with the kanji, so you should be good to go here.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means mix , so the verb vocab version is to mix something , to stir something , or to blend something . This is when someone is actively doing the mixing. You can remember this because they're ( ぜる ) doing the mixing themselves, rather than just sitting around and waiting for something to naturally mix on its own.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: The person who taught you how to mix something is your ma ( ま ). Your ma is always mixing tasty things: stew, curry, cake batter — even the occasional cocktail. She's an expert mixer, and she passed her mixing skills on to you. You can also use the level 5 vocab 交ぜる to help you remember, as it has the same meaning and reading!
